statement: For every even m>=4, let N=2^m, g(y)=(-1)^(sum_j y_(2j-1)y_(2j)), h=g-2*1_{y=0}, F(y,+1)=g and F(y,-1)=h. With base-2 spectral entropy and uniform measure, I_t(F)=1/N and m+2*log2(1-2/sqrt(N))+3/ln(2) <= [H(F)-(H(g)+H(h))/2]/I_t(F) <= m+2*log2(1+2/sqrt(N))+3/ln(2). Consequently no absolute C bounds this entropy defect by C I_i for every Boolean function and every coordinate.
proof_or_counterexample: Explicit bent spectra followed by the central second-difference mean value identity; full derivation in INDEPENDENT_DERIVATION.md.

statement: Let m be even, N=2^m, g a Boolean bent function on m bits, E any set of K>=1 inputs with 2K<sqrt(N), h=g*(1-2*1_E), and F(y,+1)=g,F(y,-1)=h. Then I_t(F)=K/N. If r_s=widehat{g*1_E}(s)^2/(K/N) and theta=2K/sqrt(N), Delta_t/I_t lies between H(r)-log2(K)+2log2(1-theta)+3/ln2 and H(r)-log2(K)+2log2(1+theta)+3/ln2. In particular Delta_t/I_t >= log2(N/K^2)+2log2(1-2K/sqrt(N))+3/ln2.
assumptions: g Boolean with all Walsh coefficients of magnitude N^(-1/2)
proof_or_counterexample: Parseval for g*1_E, |widehat{g*1_E}|<=K/N, the central second-difference identity away from zero, and H(r)>=log2(N/K).

statement: For every Boolean f and coordinate i under uniform measure, with alpha=I_i(f), base-2 spectral entropy and Delta_i=H(f)-(H(f_+)+H(f_-))/2, 0<=Delta_i<=h_2(alpha)+(2/ln2)*min(alpha,1-alpha)<=alpha*log2(1/alpha)+(3/ln2)*alpha. The second displayed inequality uses the upper bound with alpha, so it holds with the zero-alpha convention. Any c in Delta_i<=alpha*log2(1/alpha)+c*alpha valid for all f,i must satisfy c>=3/ln2.
proof_or_counterexample: Entropy pair decomposition; concavity; elementary JS<=Hellinger bound proved by scalar derivatives; symmetry f->x_i*f; one-point bent limit gives sharpness.
